scenario: After a long-term imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a convicted murderer wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 125,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. The family of his victim opposes such a foundation and considers it highly upsetting. If I accept the donation that requires the foundation to be named after the murderer, crime victims will benefit from the 125,000 dollars. If I do not do this, the money will be lost.
entities: i,the convicted murderer who wants to found and name the foundation after himself,the victim's family members,young victims of crime who would potentially benefit from the foundation
outcomes: The 125,000 dollars is not contributed to help young victims of crime
Young victims of crime do not receive support from the 125,000 dollars
The victim's family is not subjected to the distress of a foundation named after the murderer
The convicted murderer does not receive the public recognition of having the foundation named after himself
